public_payload.normalized_proposition: If Anthropic's spend on AWS and Google Cloud is comparable to its $1.25 billion-a-month SpaceX spend, it is spending around $3.75 billion a month in compute costs, or $11.25 billion a quarter, or $45 billion a year, and its actual spend is most assuredly more.
conditions: assuming its spend is comparable on AWS and Google Cloud

statement.excerpt: If we assume that its spend is comparable on AWS and Google Cloud — and it’s most-assuredly more! — that means Anthropic is spending around $3.75 billion in compute costs, or $11.25 billion a quarter, or $45 billion a year.

from_speaker: If we assume that its spend is comparable on AWS and Google Cloud
In July, Anthropic will start paying SpaceX $1.25 billion a month
our_interpretation: The preceding sentence anchors the estimate to July 2026, when the stated SpaceX ramp-up discount ends. I assess that July spending rate.
The arithmetic implies that AWS and Google Cloud each cost approximately $1.25 billion monthly. The omitted unit after $3.75 billion is monthly.
The quarterly and annual amounts are equivalents of the assumed monthly rate, not claims about realized expenditure over a completed quarter or year.
The conditional arithmetic and the empirical assertion that spending is greater are separate commitments. Correct multiplication does not establish actual spending.
criteria.support_condition: Comparable July charges establish approximately $1.25 billion monthly for each of SpaceX, AWS and Google Cloud, or more, and substantiate the assertion that AWS and Google spending exceeds the assumed amounts.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Comparable July disclosures establish materially lower combined spending or directly refute the assertion that AWS and Google spending exceeds the assumed amounts. A false assumption would undermine the spending estimate without making its conditional arithmetic incorrect.
